name: Validation

hero.title: Write it like Zod. It won all 12 cells of our workload bench.
hero.lede: `s` is a schema library with the chain you already know, compiled to one flat function on first parse. The same schema runs light in the browser and strict on the server, and Zod, Valibot or ArkType schemas plug into every Pyreon package that takes one.

why.title: Why it is worth a new import.

items.title: Fast where forms and APIs live
items.text: Each schema compiles to one monomorphic function the first time it parses. Rejecting bad input, which every form and endpoint does all day, is where it is strongest: in the 10-library bench it never loses an invalid-input parse.

items.title: Light in the browser, strict on the server
items.text: Import `@pyreon/validate/server` on the server and every `.email()` and `.phone()` upgrades to strict RFC 5322 and full E.164, with a disposable-domain blocklist. None of that code reaches the client bundle.

items.title: Checks that need your database
items.text: `.serverCheck('email-unique')` passes in the browser and is listed in `r.pending` so the UI can say "checking". On the server, `parseAsync` runs the check you registered. One schema, no second copy.

items.title: Errors ready to translate
items.text: Every issue carries a `code`, an i18n `key` like `validate.string.email` and its `params`. `formatErrorsByPath(issues, t)` turns them into one message per field, in any language.

difference.title: One schema for both sides, and the browser knows what it skipped.

before.label: Zod, a database check
before.caption: A second schema for the server, so the DB call stays out of the bundle. The two drift, and the client never learns a check is pending.

after.label: with @pyreon/validate
after.caption: The check is part of the shared schema. The browser records it as pending; the server runs it, plus strict email rules.

extraSectionsHtml:
which package do I need?

One product, two packages.

Validation ships as two npm packages with similar names. Most apps install only the first.

install this

@pyreon/validate

The validator you write schemas with: s.object, s.string().email() and the rest. Plus helpers for labels, translated errors and live validation that also work on Zod, Valibot and ArkType schemas.

$ bun add @pyreon/validate
comes with forms and stores

@pyreon/validation

The plumbing. Forms, Store and State-tree use it to accept any schema, and it's installed with them. You only import it yourself for its typed Zod, Valibot or ArkType adapters.

demo.title: One schema, validated twice.
demo.text: Type an email and validate. The browser runs the light format check and lists `email-unique` as pending; the server pass runs the strict email rules, the disposable-domain blocklist and the uniqueness check. Try ada@example.com (taken) and test@mailinator.com (disposable).

demo.spec: DemoValidation uses the real `@pyreon/validate`: one `s.object({ email: s.string().email().serverCheck('email-unique') })`. The browser column shows `Signup.parse(value)` (ok/fail and the `pending` list). The server column simulates a server round-trip of about 700 ms and runs `strictEmail()` and `isDisposableEmail()` from `@pyreon/validate/server` plus a mock uniqueness check where only ada@example.com is taken. The earlier benchmark bars and bundle bars are removed: they came from a 2026-08-31 run and an unsourced size table, not the current record.

items.name: The full chain
items.text: strings, numbers, bigints, dates, literals, enums, objects, arrays, tuples, records, maps, sets, unions, discriminated unions, intersections, lazy recursion.

items.name: Refine and transform
items.text: `.refine`, `.superRefine`, `.transform`, `.pipe`, `s.preprocess`, `s.coerce`; async members work inside every composition via `parseAsync`.

items.name: Resilient parsing
items.text: `.catch(fallback)` for bad fields, `.readonly()` for frozen output.

items.name: `.is()` for a boolean
items.text: a verdict-only compiled path that builds no output and no issues.

items.name: JSON Schema out
items.text: `toJsonSchema()` emits draft 2020-12 for OpenAPI, editor autocomplete or an LLM's structured output.

items.name: Strict CSP
items.text: `configure({ jit: false })` runs the interpreter with identical results when `unsafe-eval` is off.

items.name: Labels on any schema
items.text: `withField(z.string().email(), { label, placeholder })` attaches metadata to Zod, Valibot, ArkType or `s` schemas.

items.name: Shared native schemas
items.text: A declared `s.object({...})` compiles to a native struct on iOS and Android, and its `parse` returns the same `{ ok, value, issues }` there. Experimental.

api.title: One namespace for schemas, a few helpers for the rest.

limits.title: The result shape is `{ ok }`, not `{ success }`
limits.text: `parse()` and its alias `safeParse()` return `{ ok, value }` or `{ ok, issues }` and never throw. Use `parseOrThrow()` where an exception reads better.

limits.title: Strict CSP: one line skips the JIT
limits.text: The JIT uses `new Function`. Under a CSP without `unsafe-eval` it falls back to the interpreter after one blocked attempt; call `configure({ jit: false })` at startup to skip that attempt. Results are identical, only slower.

limits.title: The chain does not tree-shake
limits.text: Chain methods live on prototypes. For the smallest bundle import from `@pyreon/validate/mini`, or let `pyreon({ optimizeValidators: true })` rewrite module-level schemas for you.

limits.title: A browser `ok` is not the final word
limits.text: `.serverCheck` always passes in the browser and shows up in `pending`. Treat the server's `parseAsync` as the verdict.

related.name: Forms
related.text: Pass a schema straight to useForm.

related.name: Store
related.text: `defineSchemaStore` validates every `set` and `patch` against a schema.

end.title: Keep the chain. Lose the second schema.

comingFrom.title: Rename `z` to `s`, read `ok` instead of `success`.
comingFrom.note: The chain is the same for the common cases. Or keep Zod: Pyreon's form, store and state-tree accept a Zod schema as it is.

comingFrom.title: Same functional style, same tree-shaking, from `/mini`.
comingFrom.note: From the next release `@pyreon/validate/mini` ships without the runtime JIT; call `enableJit()` from `@pyreon/validate/jit` once if you want its speed back.

recipes.title: Error messages in German, from the issue keys
recipes.text: Every built-in issue has an i18n key and params, so translation is a lookup, not a regex over English text.

recipes.title: A schema an LLM or an OpenAPI spec can read
recipes.text: Emit JSON Schema from the same object you validate with, then check what comes back.

recipes.title: Validate a signal as it changes
recipes.text: `parseReactive` gives a computed result for templates; `watchValid` calls you only when validity flips.

faq.q: Where does it lose, and why?
faq.a: Six of 24 protocol cells: Zod's compiled mode parses a valid email, int and 20-item array faster; ArkType parses a valid user object faster because it hands back your input instead of a clean copy; typia and ArkType check emails faster. On email the grammars also differ: ArkType accepts `a..b@x.com` and `a@-x.com`, which Zod, Valibot and `s` reject.

No. We wrote the bench, it is synthetic, and the validate rows are one run on one machine. Every library is checked for identical results before timing. Run it yourself: `cd packages/fundamentals/validate && bun bench/validation.ts`.

Install `@pyreon/validate`: it is the `s` schema library plus helpers. `@pyreon/validation` is the small adapter layer (`zodSchema`, `valibotSchema`, `arktypeSchema`, the Standard Schema bridge) that forms, stores and state trees use to accept any validator. It comes with them.

faq.q: Do I have to switch from Zod?
faq.a: No. `withField`, `parseReactive`, `formatErrors` and every Pyreon package that takes a schema work with a Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema directly. Switch when the speed or the server split is worth it to you.
`.refine` and `.transform` can be async anywhere in the tree; call `parseAsync`. A sync `parse()` of an async schema returns one issue telling you to use `parseAsync`, instead of a wrong answer.
